contract: The shape a PluginManifest has AFTER Rust re-serializes it, on its way back to the frontend (read_manifest_at for dev-folder plugins; PluginManifest embedded in InstalledPluginInfo). Rust deserializes `input` into PluginManifest, serializes it, and must get `serialized`. The vitest side feeds `serialized` straight to validateManifest, which must accept it. Neither side transcribes the other's expectations by hand: add a field to PluginManifest and the Rust test fails here first, and updating this file is what tells the frontend test what now crosses the boundary. `input` is owned by this fixture and is not tied to any shipped manifest — it was first written by copying examples/plugins/ai-summary/baram-plugin.json, but that plugin is expected to gain a `contributions` key once declarative sidebar contributions exist, and the absence of that key is the whole point here. The case being pinned: a manifest that declares no `contributions` used to arrive as an explicit null and be rejected as 'contributions must be an object'.

input.name: AI Summary
input.description: Summarizes the current document with AI, in a sidebar panel; caches the last summary.
